ordered_diagnoses: Corrected transposition of the great arteries

s1.syndrome_frame: Acute chest pain with vomiting and abnormal cardiac findings
salient_findings: ST-segment elevations in multiple ECG leads
key_facts: Patient is a man in his 80s
Chest pain duration is 1 hour
Patient denies history of hypertension and diabetes
Temperature is 36°C
Heart rate is 79 beats per minute
Blood pressure is 92/56 mm Hg
Maximal cardiac impulse is in the right fifth interspace
Hepatic dullness is located in the left subcostal region
Initial serum troponin I level is 0.070 ng/mL
ECG shows negative P waves in lead I
ECG shows QRS complexes with activation of ventricle in right thorax
Coronary Angiography shows total occlusion in the proximal right coronary artery
Transthoracic Echocardiogram shows right atrium and right ventricle on the left side, and left atrium and left ventricle on the right side

shortlist.label: Acute myocardial infarction
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated serum troponin I level and total occlusion in the proximal right coronary artery

shortlist.label: Right ventricular infarction
shortlist.why_kept: ST-segment elevations in leads I, II, III, aVF, and V4 through V6, and total occlusion in the proximal right coronary artery

shortlist.label: Dextrocardia with situs inversus
shortlist.why_kept: Maximal cardiac impulse in the right fifth interspace and hepatic dullness in the left subcostal region, suggesting abnormal cardiac positioning

shortlist.label: Corrected transposition of the great arteries
shortlist.why_kept: Transthoracic Echocardiogram showing right atrium and right ventricle on the left side, and left atrium and left ventricle on the right side

shortlist.label: Arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy
shortlist.why_kept: ECG findings of negative P waves in lead I and QRS complexes with activation of ventricle in right thorax, suggesting possible right ventricular dysfunction

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation with chest pain, vomiting, and elevated troponin levels, combined with the ECG findings of ST-segment elevations and the coronary angiography showing total occlusion in the proximal right coronary artery, are consistent with a right ventricular infarction. The location of the maximal cardiac impulse in the right fifth interspace and the hepatic dullness in the left subcostal region also suggest right ventricular involvement.

rejected.label: Acute myocardial infarction
rejected.why: While the patient has elevated troponin levels and ECG changes, the specific findings suggest a more localized right ventricular infarction rather than a general acute myocardial infarction.

rejected.label: Dextrocardia with situs inversus
rejected.why: The transthoracic echocardiogram shows the right atrium and ventricle on the left side, which is not consistent with dextrocardia with situs inversus, where the heart would be on the right side.

rejected.label: Corrected transposition of the great arteries
rejected.why: This condition would not typically present with acute chest pain and infarction, and the echocardiogram findings do not support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy
rejected.why: While this condition can cause right ventricular dysfunction, the patient's presentation with acute chest pain and infarction is more consistent with a right ventricular infarction rather than a chronic cardiomyopathy.
